subject.title: [Feature]: Cron should distinguish execution success from delivery failure and show warning instead of error

question: Should cron partial-success runs be persisted as a new `warning` CronRunStatus, or should execution remain `ok` while Control UI derives a warning presentation from `deliveryStatus=not-delivered`?
rationale: Both approaches solve the reported operator confusion, but adding a new status value changes public protocol/client unions while deriving the warning from delivery fields preserves the existing execution-status contract.

options.title: Derive warning from delivery fields
options.body: Keep `CronRunStatus` as execution-only and render `ok` plus failed delivery metadata as a warning in UI/API presentation where needed.

options.title: Add first-class warning status
options.body: Land a broader additive protocol/UI change that records `warning` as a persisted cron run status and updates every repo-owned client surface.

options.title: Defer until linked bug PRs settle
options.body: Pause this issue until the narrower delivery-failure PRs prove whether `ok + deliveryStatus` is sufficient for users.

recommendation.title: Derive warning from delivery fields
recommendation.body: Keep `CronRunStatus` as execution-only and render `ok` plus failed delivery metadata as a warning in UI/API presentation where needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron runtime and protocol refactors make this the best available routing candidate for the status-contract decision.
